overview.body:
**Lono** ​(*lono*) — ‌Agriculture, ‌Peace, Rain ​· ​Hawaiian deity, ​associated ​with fertility, ​agriculture, ‌rainfall, music ​and ​peace — ‌belongs ​to the ‌Polynesian ​tradition, where ‌it ​is catalogued ​under ​the domain ​"Agriculture, ​Peace, Rain". ‌The ​name means ‌"Hawaiian ​deity, associated ‌with ​fertility, agriculture, ‌rainfall, ​music and ‌peace".

​**Lono** is ​agriculture, ‌peace, rain. ‌The ‌name means ​"Hawaiian ​deity, associated ‌with ​fertility, agriculture, ​rainfall, ‌music and ​peace" ​and belongs ‌to ​the polynesian ‌tradition.

​PuniCodex restores ​the ​name as ​**Lono** ‌and serves ‌its ​temple at ‌[its ​temple](https://punicodex.com/lono/). The ​restoration ‌needs no ‌distinctive ‌letters or ‌diacritics ​its ASCII ‌form ​would lose, ​which ​places the ‌name ​in Tier ​2. ​The plain ‌ASCII ​form *lono* ​survives ​as a ‌modern ​convenience imposed ‌by ​the early ‌domain-name ​system; the ‌restoration, ‌not the ​fallback, ​is the ​form ​the project ‌defends ‌as philologically ​complete.

the-name.body:
The ​name is ‌attested ‌in ​modern Polynesian ​orthographies; ​macron ​usage follows ​each ‌tradition’s ​reference dictionaries. ​Etymologically ‌the ​name means ‌"Hawaiian ​deity, ‌associated with ​fertility, ​agriculture, rainfall, ​music ​and ​peace".

The ‌ASCII ​form ‌*lono* survives ​only ‌because ​the early ‌domain-name ​system ‌could not ​carry ​diacritics; ‌it is ‌a ‌technological compromise, ​not ​an ‌ancient spelling. ​The ​Unicode ‌restoration **Lono** ​recovers ​the ‌full diacritic ​detail ‌of ​the scholarly ​transliteration ​directly ​in the ‌address ‌bar. ​The restoration ‌needs ​no distinctive ​letters ‌or ‌diacritics its ‌ASCII ‌form ​would lose, ‌which ​places ​the name ​in ‌Tier ​2.

The ​letter-by-letter ​transformation ‌runs:

- ​**l** ​→ **L** ​— ‌Same, ​capitalized
- ‌**o** ​→ ‌**o** — ​Same
‌- ‌**n** → ​**n** ​— ​Same
- ​**o** ‌→ ‌**o** — ​Same

pronunciation.body:
The ​reconstructed ‌pronunciation of ‌the ​name ​is ​**/lono/** — ​Restored ​scholarly ‌form.

​Phoneme by ​phoneme:

‌- ​**lono** ‌— ​The canonical ‌restored ​form ​Lono.

​For the ​modern ​speaker, ‌the ​closest approximation ‌is: ​Say ‌"lono" ​with the ‌stress ​and ‌length ​implied by ​the ‌scholarly ‌restoration ‌"Lono".

​The ASCII ​form ‌"lono" ​is ​a DNS ‌compromise; ​the ​restoration ‌"Lono" preserves ​the ‌name's ​scholarly ​dignity.

The ​pronunciation ​given ‌above ‌reconstructs the ​sound ‌world ​in ​which ‌Lono was ‌invoked. ‌Modern ‌speakers ​should not ‌expect ​exact ​identity ​with ancient ‌phonology; ​the ​reconstruction ​is a ‌scholarly ​compass, ​not ​a performance ‌prescription. ​The ‌restoration ​Lono ‌keeps the ​prosodic ‌information ‌visible ​even when ​the ​name ​is ‌typed in ‌plain ​ASCII.

mythology.body:
The ​stories of ‌Lono ‌place agriculture, ​peace, ​rain at ​the ​center of ​a ‌living mythological ​world.

​### ‌Origins (Myth)

​Lono ‌appears in ​polynesian ‌tradition as ​agriculture, ​peace, rain. ​The ​name's meaning, ​"Hawaiian ‌deity, associated ​with ‌fertility, agriculture, ​rainfall, ‌music and ​peace", ‌shapes the ​narratives ‌told about ​this ​figure.

### ‌Worship ‌and ‌Memory (Cult)

​Devotees ​and later ‌tradition-keepers ​preserved Lono ​in ‌ritual, text, ​and ​iconography, ensuring ‌the ​name survived ‌into ​the modern ​scholarly ​record.

The ​myths ‌of Lono ‌survive ​in fragments, ‌summaries, ​and ​later retellings. ‌Each ‌version reflects ‌the ‌interests of ​its ‌tellers — ​poets, ​priests, philosophers, ​and ‌scholars. The ​PuniCodex ​entry does ​not ‌privilege a ​single ​version; it ​gathers ‌the attestations ​so ‌that readers ​can ‌compare ​them. The ‌restoration ‌Lono gives ​the ​figure a ​stable ​name around ‌which ‌these variants ​orbit.

archaeology.body:
No ​monument, ‌inscription, ‌or ​artifact in ​the ​current ​PuniCodex ​corpus ‌is ​yet ​assigned to ‌Lono ​with ‌certainty. ​That ‌absence ​should ​be read ​honestly: ​for ​a ‌Polynesian ​name ‌of ​this ‌type the ​material ‌record ​is ‌expected ​to ​be ‌thin, and ‌the ‌primary ​evidence ​remains ‌the ​textual ​testimony gathered ‌in ​the ​Scholarly ‌Sources ​section.

‌Were ​such ​evidence to ​surface, ​it ‌would ‌take ​recognizable ‌forms: ​votive or ​dedicatory ‌inscriptions ‌naming ‌Lono, ‌sanctuary ​or ‌cult remains ​tied ​to ​agriculture ‌and ​iconography ​matching ​its ‌traditional attributes ​(name ​and ​domain). ‌Each ​candidate ‌would ​be weighed ‌against ​the ‌reconstructed ‌form ​of ​the ​name before ​entering ‌the ‌scholarly ​record.

meditation.body:
To ​contemplate Lono ‌is ‌to ​hold the ​idea ​of agriculture, ​Peace, ​Rain ‌in the ​mind ​and to ‌ask ​what ‌of it ​endures. ‌The name ​means ​"Hawaiian ​deity, associated ​with ​fertility, agriculture, ‌rainfall, ​music ‌and peace" ​— ‌and a ​name ‌that ​carries its ‌meaning ​so openly ​invites ‌meditation ‌rather than ‌mere ​recollection. The ​tradition ‌remembers ​the name ​as ‌agriculture, Peace, ​Rain ​· ‌Hawaiian deity, ​associated ‌with ​fertility, agriculture, ​rainfall, ​music and ​peace.

‌Sit ‌with the ​restored ‌form — ​Lono ​— ‌and the ‌diacritics ‌themselves become ‌the ​practice: ‌each mark ​is ​a small ​act ‌of ​attention, a ​refusal ​to let ‌the ​plain ​ASCII form ​*lono* ‌stand in ​for ‌the ​whole. What ‌the ​tradition preserved ‌in ‌this ​name, the ​restoration ​asks the ​reader ‌to ‌preserve in ​turn.
